picks.file: Vesontio Sequanorum Gallis Besanson Germanis Bysantz - btv1b531789878 (1 of 2).jpg
picks.what: Bird’s-eye view, engraving in Braun and Hogenberg, Civitates Orbis Terrarum, vol. 2
picks.why: colored, flat loose sheet (no gutter): the town in the loop of the Doubs under the citadel hill; trimmed sheet margins and library stamp

picks.what: General view from the Vesoul road, lithograph (British Museum)
picks.who: Isidore Laurent Deroy and Victor Adam
picks.why: whole town in its valley with the Doubs, a bridge and the citadel on its height; trimmed mount, plate number and caption

picks.file: The swing bridge and Madeleine church, Besançon, France-LCCN2001697579.jpg
picks.what: The Battant bridge and the Madeleine church, photochrom print (Library of Congress)
picks.why: the old bridge over the Doubs and the twin-towered Madeleine, a classic Besançon scene; color, landscape

picks.what: The old town from the Fort de Chaudanne, photograph
picks.why: broad sunny view over the red roofs of the old town inside the river loop

gaps: P0, P2: no candidates. P5: none (the Mittelholzer aerials #17–#20 are of a factory on the Rue de Besançon in Pontarlier, not Besançon).
notes: #4: BnF dates its copy 1645 (a later printing); the plate is from vol. 2, first published 1575. Other copies of the same plate are bound-book photos with the gutter through the view (#1, #2, #3 in black and white) or show the center fold (#6). P3 alternative: #9 (Bichebois, 1827), the citadel above the Tour de la Pelote from the ramparts — same lithograph series, closer view. P4: #11/#15 (‘General view, with the Doubs’) is a wide view but shows neither the citadel nor the cathedral; #12 is a Flickr copy of #14. Not Besançon: #8 (Saint-Wandrille abbey, Normandy, painting in the Besançon museum), #16 (portrait).
